draft.title: The biosphere
card: The biosphere is all living things on Earth and the places where they live. It includes plants, animals, fungi and microbes, on land, in water and in the air close to the surface.
Living things depend on the other three spheres. They need gases from the atmosphere, water from the hydrosphere, and soil and minerals from the lithosphere.
The biosphere is made of ecosystems. Each one is a community of living things and the non-living surroundings they depend on, such as a coral reef or a desert.
Life also acts on the other spheres. Plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen, and roots and microbes help build soil.
draft.remember: The biosphere is life and its habitats, and it relies on air, water and rock.

a.q: Which description best fits the biosphere?
opts: All living things and the places they live
All the gases that surround the Earth
All the water found on and under the Earth
The solid rock of the crust and upper mantle
a.why: The biosphere is made of living things and their habitats. The other options describe the atmosphere, the hydrosphere and the lithosphere, which are non-living spheres that life depends on.
a.clue: Look for the sphere defined by life.

b.q: A wetland in the Riverina dries out in a long drought, and the frogs and waterbirds that lived there die or leave. Which statement best explains this in terms of the spheres?
opts: The biosphere depends on water from the hydrosphere
The hydrosphere depends on the frogs and waterbirds
The biosphere has no link to the other spheres
The lithosphere gave the frogs their water supply
b.why: The wetland's living things needed water, which comes from the hydrosphere, so losing it harmed the biosphere. The reverse is wrong: the loss of water caused the loss of life, not the other way round.
b.clue: Ask which sphere the animals needed and lost.

a.best: All living things and the places they live

b.best: The biosphere depends on water from the hydrosphere

problems.detail: The fourth bullet ('Life also acts on the other spheres... plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen, and roots and microbes help build soil') explains how the biosphere changes the other spheres. That is the flow of matter between spheres, which belongs to point 5 (How the spheres interact), so it should only be mentioned here, not taught.
